verdict.rationale: Ellis Porter publishes open educational content on the National Interest Waiver, a self-petition route it markets to founders. This includes a public step-by-step NIW journey page, an open NIW article on premium processing, and guidance pages listing red flags and questions to ask a firm. However, the content centers on NIW and firm services rather than startup visas broadly, and no criteria breakdowns or real case examples are shown. Missing for 10: startup-visa-specific guides (e.g., O-1/E-2/entrepreneur paths for founders), detailed criteria breakdowns, real-world case examples, evidence of guide depth and volume, independent corroboration that the content is ungated.

support.subject: As a founder, the provider publishes substantial free guides on startup visas — criteria breakdowns, process explainers, real examples — open to anyone, not gated lead bait

citations.quote: Publishes premium-processing guidance: "NIW premium processing: what it speeds up" among its open NIW articles.
The National Interest Waiver lets you petition for a green card on your own when your work serves the national interest of the United States. No employer sponsorship and no job offer required.
no employer needs to be involved, there's no job offer to maintain, you're free to change jobs without affecting your case
